title: Dreaming Back to Those Years
next_chapter_hook: The woman's face gradually came into focus, and the contours so strikingly similar to Su Qingyao sent a chill of bone-deep cold through Chen Ji's heart—if she was the one who murdered his father, then what was all his trust in her over the years worth?

text.content: The moment his fingertips touched the rune, a chilling energy surged directly into his Mental Sea along his meridians. Chen Ji felt his vision go black as he plunged into an abyss without bottom, surrounded by chaotic gray-white mist. 'This is...' He instinctively tried to struggle, only to find his four limbs bound by invisible chains, unable to move. The Turtle Shell floated in the void, runes transforming into golden light particles that circled his body, while those never-before-seen symbols rearranged themselves in an ancient and unfamiliar pattern. A violent bout of vertigo struck, and Chen Ji forced himself to maintain consciousness clarity, yet his heart was turbulent like stormy seas—these runes had never appeared on his father's Testament Letter, so why were they manifesting now?

The gray-white mist gradually dissipated, replaced by a field of withered reeds. The autumn wind was bleak, reed catkins drifted like snow, and a turbid yellow river wound through the land, its banks scattered with moss-covered stones. Chen Ji stood frozen on the spot—this place was unmistakably the old ruins of Tianqing Sect Back Mountain! As a child, he had visited here with his father, those memories now faded and vague. Seeing this scene with his own eyes, his heart inexplicably tightened. In the distance came the faint sound of clashing weapons, mixed with several angry shouts. Chen Ji's pupils constricted—that voice, though distant, was uncannily familiar, making his scalp tingle.

'Ji'er...' An elderly yet gentle voice sounded in his ear. Chen Ji's body trembled violently as he spun around. No one stood behind him, only the reeds swaying in the wind, yet the call was so vivid, as if his father stood right behind him, within reach. 'That's impossible...' Chen Ji murmured to himself, his fingertips trembling slightly. After years of cultivating the Tianji Record, he had never encountered such a bizarre situation—this was clearly not foresight of the future, but rather... a regression into the past. Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly rang in his mind: 'This is the memory regression function of the Tianji Record, the cost is Heavenly Fate Value consumption. Lad, are you certain you want to continue watching?'

dialogue.content: 'Since it has already been triggered, there is no turning back.' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a weight of solemnity, 'But this old man must remind you—once the memories of the past are fully seen, you can no longer pretend ignorance. Think carefully, the Heavenly Fate Value consumption for this scroll is no small amount.'

choice.prompt: Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed in his ears, Chen Ji clenched his fists tightly. Pursue the truth, or give up here and now?

choices.description: Father's death cannot remain unclear and unexamined, even if it means paying the price of Heavenly Fate Value, I must see the complete truth.
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate Value will be consumed again, possibly triggering unknown consequences

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, his gaze gradually firming. No matter how cruel the truth, he must see it with his own eyes—this was not only for his father, but also to find an answer for all his forbearance and scheming over these years. 'I have seen.' His voice was low and calm, 'Continue.'

choices.description: Now is not the time to investigate the past, hidden currents churn within the sect, one must not sacrifice the greater for the lesser. Preserving strength is the best strategy.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the mystery, do not expose attention to the past
choices.risk_hint: May permanently lose this opportunity for regression

text.content: A flash of struggle flickered in Chen Ji's eyes, but quickly returned to his usual composure. The time is not yet ripe—with both internal and external troubles plaguing the Tianqing Sect, exposure from investigating past matters would be a losing proposition. Just as he was about to speak and request exiting the regression, the scene before him abruptly accelerated, forcibly dragging him into a deeper vortex of memories...

The scene suddenly sharpened. In the reeds, three dark figures had surrounded a man in blue robes. The man faced away from Chen Ji, his figure gaunt yet straight as a pine, holding a scroll of yellowed bamboo in his hand—that was precisely the page of the Tianji Record Chen Ji had seen on the Turtle Shell not long ago. 'Chen Xuan, hand over the Tianji Record smartly!' The leading dark figure shouted harshly, voice hoarse and jarring, 'Our master above values you somewhat. As long as you hand over the fragment, past wrongs will be forgiven, and we can even preserve your life!' Chen Ji's whole body shuddered—the name was his father's. Chen Xuan, so that was his father's full name!

The blue-robed man slowly turned, revealing a refined and elegant face. Time had carved fine lines at the corners of his eyes, but his brow carried an unyielding pride. His gaze was terrifyingly calm, as if he had long since transcended life and death. 'Past forgiveness?' Chen Xuan laughed lightly, his voice warm and mellow yet tinged with mockery, 'The master behind you all said the same to me back then, didn't he? Unfortunately, his words and your swords have always been equally unreliable.' Chen Ji gazed at his father's face, his throat blocked as if by something. The father in memory was always taciturn, never knowing that beneath that silence lay such unknown pride and edge.

'Preferring a forfeit to a forced toast!' The leading dark figure laughed in furious mockery, his long blade descending with murderous cold intent. Chen Xuan sidestepped, and the Tianji Record in his palm suddenly blazed with blinding golden light. Strangely, that radiance did not attack the enemies, but instead shattered the surrounding scenery into fragments. The three dark figures' expressions changed drastically as they retreated. 'What an impressive Tianji Record...' The leader gritted his teeth, 'As the rumors claimed, it can indeed foresee three hours ahead. Unfortunately, today you are destined to die here!' Chen Ji's pupils constricted. Father... Father also possessed the foresight ability of the Tianji Record? Then where did this fragment come from?

Blade light and sword shadows crisscrossed through the reeds, the scent of blood gradually thickening. Chen Xuan fought three alone, his movements agile yet clearly lacking stamina. His left shoulder had been cut, blood staining half his blue robes. 'Father!' Chen Ji instinctively cried out, knowing this was merely a phantom of the past, yet unable to restrain himself from rushing forward. However, his hands passed through his father's figure, like passing through a wisp of ethereal mist. Chen Xuan seemed to sense something, suddenly turning his head back mid-battle, his gaze passing through layers of reeds, directly toward where Chen Ji stood. His lips parted slightly, as if speaking—'Ji'er... find her...'

At that moment, a white figure darted out from within the reeds. It was a woman, dressed in a plain white long skirt, her face veiled by a wisp of gauze, revealing only a pair of crystal-clear eyes like autumn water. She held an ancient and simple Jade Pendant in her hand, muttering words. In an instant, a brilliant radiance descended from heaven, repelling all three dark figures. 'Go!' The woman's cold voice rang out as she caught the swaying Chen Xuan with one arm, her gaze revealing a hint of anxiety and heartache. Chen Ji stared fixedly at that figure, his heartbeat nearly stopping. That outline, that aura—why was it so familiar?

choice.prompt: The woman's appearance reversed the battle's situation, but Chen Ji could not see her face clearly. That inexplicable sense of familiarity left him completely unsettled—exactly who was she?

choices.description: That figure bears such a striking resemblance to Su Qingyao, but it's still too early to draw conclusions. Wait for the moment she turns around.

text.content: Chen Ji clenched his teeth, focusing all his spiritual energy on his vision. He wanted to see that woman's face with his own eyes—if she truly was... Yet just at this moment, the image violently distorted, as if some force had forcibly severed the memory, plunging it into endless darkness and chaos.

choices.description: Cannot jump to conclusions based solely on a silhouette. Perhaps just someone similar, or a trap set by enemies.
choices.visible_reward: Stay Calm and Analyze the Situation

text.content: Chen Ji forced himself to remain calm. He couldn't let a vague figure throw him into confusion—how many similar-looking people exist in this world? Yet the image seemed to sense his hesitation, pushing forward on its own, freezing at the moment the woman turned around—

In the instant the light silk was blown aside by the wind, a coldly beautiful face emerged beneath the sunset's afterglow.

It was a face of devastating beauty, with brows like distant mountains, eyes like cold stars, and lips slightly pursed, carrying an innate pride and aloofness. She helped Chen Xuan retreat into the depths of the reeds, casting one final glance back—

In that instant, Chen Ji felt his heart gripped tightly by an invisible hand.

It was Su Qingyao. That was unmistakably Su Qingyao!

But... how could this be? Su Qingyao is barely over twenty now, yet the one in the image appeared to be of marriageable age. If this truly depicts the scene of his father's ambush, that would have been at least twenty years ago...

"Impossible..." Chen Ji murmured, retreating, his mind churning with waves of shock. "Su Qingyao... why would she appear in my father's memories? Was she the one who saved my father, or..."

The image twisted violently once more. Three dark silhouettes closed in, and Chen Xuan thrust the Tianji Record into the woman's embrace, his voice urgent yet clear: "Take it and go! Find my child... Chen Ji... Raise him to adulthood..."

"What about you?" The woman's voice trembled slightly.

Chen Xuan turned to face the enemies, his back resolute and solitary: "I'll hold them off."

He paused, as if sensing something, and abruptly looked back, lips parting—

"Ji'er, the Tianji Record will guide you. Trust no one... including her."

Before the words faded, the image collapsed completely.

Chen Ji felt the world spinning, as if torn from the memory by some immense force. He snapped his eyes open to find himself still kneeling on the floor, cold sweat having soaked through his back.

The turtle shell lay quietly in his palm, those runes now dim, as if they had never appeared.

"Trust no one... including her." His father's dying warning echoed in his ears, while that face identical to Su Qingyao lodged itself like a thorn deep in his heart.

If that woman truly was Su Qingyao... then all these years she's been approaching him—was it coincidence, or does she have ulterior motives?

dialogue.content:
"You've seen what you wanted to see." Mo Xiansheng's voice drifted up leisurely. "But this old man must tell you—the Tianji Record's memory regression is not complete. It often only reveals the tip of the iceberg. That woman's identity may not be as simple as you think."

Chen Ji looked up sharply: "What do you mean?"

Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment: "This old man can only tell you—every successor of the Tianji Record has a 'Guardian' by their side. As for who she is... you'll have to discover that yourself."

text.content:
Chen Ji gripped the turtle shell tightly, his knuckles white from the force. He closed his eyes, forcing himself to regain composure.

Don't panic. How many similar-looking people exist in this world? Perhaps that woman and Su Qingyao simply happen to bear a resemblance. But his father特意留下 warning... this was by no means idle talk.

He took a deep breath, stood up, and walked to the window. Night had deepened, moonlight fell like frost, and the outline of Tianqing Sect appeared exceptionally serene in the darkness.

"Su Qingyao..." Chen Ji murmured the name softly, his heart filled with mingled emotions. Over these past days, she had tested him again and again, and again and again he had deflected her. Was she an enemy, or... the 'Guardian' his father spoke of?

choice.prompt: In the dead of night, Chen Ji stood alone at the window. His father's warning and that woman's face intertwined in his mind—how should he face Su Qingyao tomorrow?

choices.description: Since there's a lead, don't wait passively. Use roundabout methods to test whether she knows something.
choices.risk_hint: If She Truly Is an Enemy, It Would Expose Your Investigation

text.content:
A meaningful smile curved the corners of Chen Ji's lips. Since there's a direction, what comes next is designing a perfect probe.

He opened the hidden compartment by his bed, retrieving a jade pendant left by his father—a family heirloom of the Chen bloodline, inscribed with runes only the Chen family could activate. If Su Qingyao truly was connected to the events of that year, seeing this jade pendant would inevitably cause her to reveal a flaw.

choices.text: 暂时按兵不动 - Remain Temporarily Unmoved
choices.description: Before gathering more evidence, we cannot act rashly. Continue pretending to know nothing, secretly collect intelligence.
choices.visible_reward: Stay safe, don't expose our trump cards
choices.risk_hint: May continue to be kept in the dark

text.content:
Chen Ji placed the Jade Pendant back into the Hidden Compartment, his gaze gradually regaining its former depth and tranquility.

Don't be impatient. The more things are like this, the more composed one must remain. If Su Qingyao truly is an enemy, recklessly probing would only alert the target; if she really is some kind of "Guardian," then there must be reasons behind her years of protection.

In any case, the chess game continues, and Chen Ji has never lacked patience.

Suddenly, a soft footstep sounded from outside the window. Chen Ji's eyes sharpened, and he quickly gathered his thoughts, hiding the Turtle Shell in his chest. The footsteps paused outside the door for a moment, then faded away.

He walked to the door and looked down—a withered reed leaf had somehow appeared on the threshold, a species only found in the reed marsh he remembered.

Chen Ji bent down to pick up the reed leaf, his fingertips growing cold. Someone was watching him, and moreover... they came without shadow, without trace, not even察觉到他. Even he hadn't sensed them.

"It seems the waters of Tianqing Sect run deeper than I imagined." he murmured to himself, tucking the reed leaf into his sleeve. He turned back to the bed.

Tonight would be sleepless, but Chen Ji knew that from this moment on, everything had changed. His father's death, that mysterious woman, Su Qingyao's true identity... all the mysteries would be unraveled soon.

Just as he was about to fall asleep, a gentle guqin melody suddenly drifted in from the window. The music was mournful and lingering, like sobs and complaints, as if telling an ancient and sorrowful story.

Chen Ji's eyes snapped open, his heart racing. This melody... he had heard it countless times in dreams—it was his mother's favorite piece.

He rose abruptly and pushed open the window, gazing outward. Under the moonlight, a white figure stood on a distant pavilion, fingers gently stroking an ancient zither, black silk hair swaying in the wind. She seemed to sense Chen Ji's gaze and tilted her head slightly—

That silhouette, that aura, was strikingly similar to the woman who had saved his father in his memory.

"Su Qingyao..." Chen Ji murmured, his voice carrying a tremor he himself hadn't noticed.

The white figure seemed to smile, then turned and vanished into the night, as if never having appeared.

Chen Ji stood motionless before the window for a long time, his father's testament letter echoing in his mind: "Trust no one... including her."

But if she really was the woman who had saved his father more than twenty years ago... how could she possibly become his enemy?

Moonlight fell like water across Chen Ji's lean face. He slowly closed his eyes, his fists clenching and unclenching.

"Whoever you are, I will find out the truth." he said quietly, his voice carrying an undeniable resolve, "My father's vengeance, I will definitely avenge."

The night wind brushed past, carrying traces of lingering guqin melody. That woman's figure appeared especially ethereal under the moonlight, like a riddle forever beyond reach.
